facts.text: CPSO board approved amendments Oct. 13, 2026 requiring 'safer supply' and 'no carries' on prescriptions, supporting supervised consumption
Safer supply may be prescribed only with opioid agonist therapy and an in-person assessment at least monthly
CPSO expects physicians to comply by Nov. 16, 2026
A previously considered eight-week prescribing limit was dropped from the approved changes
CPSO says the amendments do not prohibit safer supply prescribing
Board heard diversion of hydromorphone is occurring, but no data quantifies how much street supply comes from safer supply
More than 87 per cent of safer supply patients are also on OAT (ODPRN data cited by board member Peter Wiesner)
North Bay police say the changes will 'pretty much eliminate diversion'
Community Care and Recovery Act, 2024 sets a 200-m buffer for injection sites near schools and requires provincial approval for municipal exemption/funding requests
CPSO proposal was reported Oct. 6, a week before the vote, building on May 2026 changes
No data establishes the clinical or diversion effect of the supervised-consumption requirement
Health Minister Sylvia Jones's office has said she supports the changes
No count of affected patients has been confirmed by the health minister's office
Peter Wiesner called for exemptions for the roughly 12 per cent of patients not on OAT
Whether exemptions for the 12 per cent were in the passed motion is not established
Board chair Dr. Patrick Safieh says the goal is preventing diversion while ensuring patients get OAT

missed.text: CPSO registrar and CEO Dr. Nancy Whitmore: 'The diversion of safer supply medication raises serious concerns for patient and public safety'
Associate registrar Dr. Anil Chopra told the board diversion information came from governments, Addiction Medicine Canada, the OMA addictions section and public health officers
Safer Municipalities Act, 2025 (passed June 2025) prohibits public consumption of illegal substances
Hydromorphone is the most common form of safer supply
